title: James O’Keefe charged after Minnesota polling station stunt | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

A Minnesota county attorney is charging right-wing influencers James O’Keefe and Cameron Higby with felony counts of unlawful voting and identity theft, alleging that the two claimed other voters’ identities while visiting polling places with concealed cameras during the state’s August primary.

Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty said O’Keefe and Higby attempted to register to vote on the day of the primary by claiming the names of real voters — some alive and some deceased. They stopped when told they would have to sign oaths to vouch for someone else’s residence and did not actually cast votes.

The influencers had been attempting to test the state’s “vouching” process, which allows a registered voter in a precinct to vouch that another person lives where they say they live. Moriarty said the system is often used by senior citizens who haven’t updated their driver’s licenses after moving into nursing homes.

“You cannot give somebody else’s name and misrepresent yourself,” Moriarty said. “Whether or not they intended to vote is irrelevant.”

The charges against the influencers come days before the November 3 midterm elections in which Democrats are aiming to topple the GOP’s House and Senate majorities.

It also comes as President Donald Trump’s administration has sent multiple states lists of what it alleges arenoncitizens on the voter rolls,intensifying its controversial efforts to stop those people from voting in the election. Trump has for years made false and disproven claims about widespread voting fraud.

The two influencers did not immediately respond to email messages seeking comment on the charges.

According to the criminal complaints, the two men disguised themselves in what O’Keefe described on X as “traditional Muslim attire.”

“We wanted to put the process to an extreme real-world test and document what election workers would tell us when confronted with the scenario firsthand,” the conservative provocateur said in asocial media postin August.

O’Keefe, 42, was the founder ofProject Veritas, a right-wing activist group that targeted journalists in sting videos that were often deceptively edited. He was fired by the Project Veritas board in 2023, and has since founded O’Keefe Media Group, where he has continued to produce videos that he claims take aim at corruption.

Moriarty added that the videos posted online of their efforts were deceptively edited.

She said election judges who were on hand raised concerns about what she described as their “strange behavior,” and flagged it to police. She said the living voters whose names O’Keefe and Higby attempted to use said they had no knowledge of their efforts.

“There’s no such thing as ‘undercover’ investigation in the polling place,” she said. “You have to identify yourself as a journalist in the polling place, which they did not.”

The two have not yet been arrested, but will be sent copies of the criminal complaint with the date of their first court appearances by the county clerk.

“This is not meant to send a message. It’s meant for these particular people to understand that what they did was unlawful,” Moriarty said.

“Minnesota’s enduring tradition of high voter turnout and excellence in elections administration is due in part to the work we all do to keep polling places as ‘islands of calm,’” Minnesota Secretary of State Steve Simon said in a statement following Moriarty’s announcement.

“These locations — our communities’ schools, churches, and senior centers – are the heart of our democracy and as such should be places of safety and peace. Any attempt to disrupt or deceive our election workers will not be tolerated.”
